proposals.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap (~6 eV), electronically insulating ionic salt that is thermodynamically stable against both the sulfide electrolyte and the LiCoO2 cathode at 4.0 V. It is a different anion family from the phosphate and borate coatings already tested, so it explores a new chemistry.
proposals.motivation: Earlier phosphate (Li3PO4) and borate (Li3BO3) coatings were tested as protective layers; a halide-family coating tests whether a more oxidation-resistant, fluoride-based insulator gives a lower interfacial penalty at 4.0 V.

proposals.hypothesis: Li3AlSiO5 is a Li-rich, wide-gap silicate built from fully oxidized Al3+ and Si4+. Neither cation is easily reduced by the Li6PS5Cl sulfide, and the silicate anion should resist oxidation at the 4.0 V LiCoO2 potential. Its high Li content should also keep it chemically compatible with the Li-rich sulfide electrolyte.
proposals.motivation: Earlier Al-silicate proposals (Li5Al(SiO4)2, LiAlSiO4) argued that Al3+ silicates resist sulfide reduction better than Ti-, Zr-, or Zn-containing candidates. Li3AlSiO5 is a Li-richer member of that Al-silicate chemistry.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate that is chemically compatible with both the sulfide electrolyte and the oxide cathode. It is a well-studied protective coating for LiCoO2 against sulfide interfacial decomposition, and its phosphate chemistry should keep the interfacial reaction penalty low at 4.0 V.

Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium borate with a low-density, weakly oxidizing B-O network. Borates are reported as protective coatings on LiCoO2 against sulfide interfacial decomposition, and this chemistry should be more stable toward the sulfide electrolyte at 4.0 V than the phosphate family already tested. This is a different anion family, so it explores a new chemistry.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 phosphate coating (mp-aaaaaegs) was evaluated as a protective layer; this proposal tests a different, borate family to compare interfacial penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap (~6 eV), electronically insulating ionic salt that is thermodynamically stable against both the sulfide electrolyte and the LiCoO2 cathode at 4.0 V. Its fluoride anion is hard to oxidize and it does not form reducible cations, so it should limit interfacial reaction penalties. It is a different anion family from the phosphate and borate coatings already tested, so it explores a new chemistry.
proposal.motivation: Earlier phosphate (Li3PO4) and borate (Li3BO3) coatings were tested as protective layers; a halide-family coating tests whether a more oxidation-resistant, fluoride-based insulator gives a lower interfacial penalty at 4.0 V.

proposal.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating silicate built from fully oxidized Al3+ and Si4+. Neither cation is easily reduced by the Li6PS5Cl sulfide, and the silicate anion is stable at the 4.0 V LiCoO2 potential. It belongs to a silicate family not yet tested, so it explores a new chemistry alongside the earlier phosphate, borate, and fluoride coatings.
proposal.motivation: Earlier coatings covered phosphate (Li3PO4), borate (Li3BO3), and fluoride (LiF) families. A silicate with Al3+ tests a different anion chemistry that may resist reduction by the sulfide better than Ti-, Zr-, or Zn-containing candidates.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a very wide-gap (~6 eV), electronically insulating, fully reduced oxide. Its O2- anion is hard to oxidize at 4.0 V, and its Li-rich composition should be thermodynamically compatible with the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte, so it should give a low interfacial penalty. It belongs to the other-oxide family, which has not been tested yet.
proposal.motivation: Earlier coatings covered phosphate, borate, fluoride, and silicate families. An other-oxide, Li-rich, fully reduced oxide tests a new chemistry that may avoid the reduction and oxidation pathways seen in the earlier choices.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2MgCl4 is a Li-rich chloride with Mg2+, a closed-shell cation that is hard to reduce. Its Cl- anion is compatible with the Cl-containing Li6PS5Cl electrolyte and is hard to oxidize at 4.0 V. It is a wide-gap, electronically insulating halide, so it should give a low interfacial penalty.
proposal.motivation: The earlier fluoride (LiF) halide coating suggested that halide chemistry may limit interfacial reactions at 4.0 V. A chloride with a non-reducible divalent cation tests whether the halide family does better with a Cl-based anion that matches the electrolyte.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlSiO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating aluminosilicate. Al3+ and Si4+ are fully oxidized and hard to reduce, so the cation chemistry should resist reduction by the Li6PS5Cl sulfide. The silicate anion should also resist oxidation at the 4.0 V LiCoO2 potential, which may keep the interfacial penalty low.
proposal.motivation: The earlier Li5Al(SiO4)2 proposal argued that an Al3+ silicate resists sulfide reduction better than Ti-, Zr-, or Zn-containing candidates. LiAlSiO4 is a closely related Al-silicate with a simpler Li-rich composition.

proposal.hypothesis: LiMgCl3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating chloride with a closed-shell Mg2+ cation that resists reduction by Li6PS5Cl. Its Cl- anion matches the chloride content of the electrolyte, and the fluoride coating already tested suggested halides may limit interfacial reactions at 4.0 V.
proposal.motivation: The earlier Li2MgCl4 proposal favored a Mg-chloride with a non-reducible divalent cation. LiMgCl3 is a closely related Li-Mg-chloride that tests the same chemistry at a different Li/Mg ratio.
